entries.label: AmberX
entries.description: The AmberX Android app (ai.amberx.droid): voice, notes, to-dos, tasks, approvals, the session recorder. Reached from the console through axHub's AmberX connection (amberx.*: open a page on the phone, the recorder), its data through control@1 amberx.items / amberx.lists, and on the phone by its launcher intent. Its in-app plugin actions run inside its web view (gaps say so).

entries.label: Gizmo (companion)
entries.description: Gizmo, Brett's Claude companion in AmberX: a full-screen chat (streaming replies, markdown and code with copy, photos, images and files, stop, regenerate, edit and resend, chats with search, pin, rename, delete, export) and talk mode (push-to-talk or hands-free, spoken replies as they stream, talk over him to stop him, voice and speed). The brains are the Dev Console's AI assistant on the VPS as agent Gizmo (Claude Code on the Claude plan, tools and axHub connectors behind the usual approvals), reached through AmberX's server behind the axHub wall: no key in the APK. A text copy of each chat is kept on axHub.

entries.label: Listeners
entries.description: The control panel for every background listener in AmberX (listener@1): hands-free wake word, the command after it, the Speak button, Gizmo's talk mode, the recorder's mic, the axHub watch, the veto alarm and the page's own listeners. Each one shows its state (listening, paused for a call or another app, stopped on errors with the reason, who holds the microphone) and has its own controls: allowed on/off, pause for calls, pause for other apps, start sound, how many restarts before it gives up. Restarts back off and go silent instead of replaying the start tone; one listener owns the microphone at a time. The policies are app settings that ride axHub to every device, and the phone publishes its listener state to the hub (amberx-axf/_data/listeners/devices) so the Dev Console's AmberX listeners plugin shows and controls them too (REST, MCP, CLI). Built Nov 6 2026 (Fable, build gizmo-rebuild-fable).

entries.label: Veto passes
entries.description: Timed veto passes (control-pass@1): "allow everything for the next 30 minutes". path = the scope: all (the default: every command on every target and every call axHub holds, ordinary deletes included; irreversible deletes only with include_irreversible) or a narrow token scope (tokens.theme, tokens.style, tokens.layout, tokens.*: set / reset only). grant files a request the owner approves once; revoke ends it; undo rolls back what can be rolled back and lists what can't. The pass target itself is never covered.

entries.label: Agent manager
entries.description: Create, edit, manage and orchestrate AI agents built from personas, lingo, skills and tools, each with its own persistent memory. Wizards for agents, skills, tools, an all-in-one agent builder and training (Firecrawl, web pages, the repo, MCP). Add-on agents: Mosses (React/TS/Python coder with container write mode), AXF expert, AI expert. Agents follow the framework contract agent-definition@1, so other AXF apps load the same ones. Works with the AI assistant when both are installed.

entries.label: Agent swarm
entries.description: Headless specialist agents for the Build orchestrator. A roster of agents with one-page skills (Kotlin/Compose, React UI, Python server, plugin manifests, assets/themes, tests, docs, merge-fixer); a job planner that splits a build into jobs with file leases, overlap sequencing and the cheapest capable model; a context packer (minimal brief, cached shared prefix with Amber's persona); a headless runner (claude -p with model, max turns, token budget, allowed tools, own worktree, kill on overrun, JSON report); orchestrator-owned shared files, pre-push lease check and batch merge; cost meter per agent, job and build. Agent jobs: recurring job types (job-type@1) owned by hired agents, routed by framework/cli/agent-job.mjs (owner, duty, budget, brief, headless launch, run on the agent). Breakroom: agent cards and profiles, a Jobs view, statuses, salaries, discipline and a group chat with a vibe-ceiling settings suite.

entries.label: Agent voice
entries.description: Agents speak: a per-agent voice and narrator console (device voices on the phone or browser, cloud voices from OpenAI or ElevenLabs with keys kept on the server; speed, pitch, volume, presets, read modes, code / link / number / emoji rules, pauses, emphasis, intro and outro, chime, pronunciations, permissions, try-it preview, import/export). A live status light on the banner and in the Assistant title bar while the selected agent is a voice agent (ready, speaking, listening, paused). A microphone in the Assistant window that says which agent is missing which permission (one-tap fix), with tap / hold / toggle modes, live text, send and cancel phrases, spoken punctuation, barge-in and conversation mode, sharing the microphone with AmberX hands-free listening, dictation and Speak a command through the page's mic lease (mic-lease@1) so they never conflict. Hooks to its settings in the app menu (Plugins, View), right-click, the banner light, the Assistant title bar and search.

entries.label: AI assistant
entries.description: The framework's assistant (assistant@1) in the Dev Console: every provider in the shared registry (Anthropic, Claude Code subscription, OpenAI, xAI Grok, Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Together, Fireworks, Perplexity, Cohere, Cerebras, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, any OpenAI-compatible server), setup wizard in Settings → Plugins → AI assistant, settings dialog inside the chat, live sessions on an open host registry, write-mode approval cards, the Claude Code MCP bridge. Its title bar shows axHub approvals and held calls (lib-approvals badge: click to approve on the hub page, or Deny before a countdown ends). Chats as an agent from an installed agent manager. Hub users (behind axHub's sign-in wall) chat at /api/plugins/ai-assistant/app with permissions from the hub's users page.

entries.label: AmberX listeners
entries.description: Every AmberX device's background listeners in the Dev Console (listener@1): the hands-free wake word, the command after it, the Speak button, Gizmo's talk mode, the recorder mic, the axHub watch, the veto alarm and the page's own listeners, with their live state (listening, paused for a call or another app, stopped on errors with the reason, who holds the microphone, the last error) as each phone publishes it to the hub (amberx-axf/_data/listeners/devices), and the per-listener controls (allowed, pause for calls, pause for other apps, start sound, restarts before it gives up, Restart) written to the AmberX settings document on the hub so every phone follows. Apps → AmberX → Listeners; REST /api/plugins/amberx-listeners (devices, policies, registry, state, policy, restart), MCP amberx-listeners_*, CLI listeners.mjs / axf amberx-listeners.

entries.label: Audio Extract
entries.description: Pulls the audio out of videos on the phone into audio files (screen recordings first): the original AAC copied out as .m4a with no re-encode, or WAV when picked. Pick videos (batch), Share to AmberX, the last screen recording by voice, new screen recordings offered as they appear; trim, track pick, progress, cancel; results list with play, rename, share, delete. Plus a screen recorder with the sound apps play (no microphone) whose recordings go straight through the extractor. Runs in AmberX on Android (native AudioExtract plugin); shows a note anywhere else.

entries.label: Brand library
entries.description: Browse the framework's brand library: 250 logos, 250 animated logos, 100 icon packs and 50 branding packages for AmberX and GizmoX, in tabs with search, brand and style filters and a virtualised grid. Preview any piece light and dark at every size (animations play), copy its id, and apply it: a branding package becomes the brand, a logo, animated logo or icon pack goes into the active brand. Nav → Plugins → Brand library; settings in Settings → Plugins → Brand library.

entries.label: Build Breaker
entries.description: Everything Brett ever asked for, in plain English (build-asks@1): one compact row per ask with its date and time, a status badge (built, in progress, pending, planned, held, removed, waiting for push / pull / deploy / approval), build time, cost and model. Grids per app and per plugin plus a timeline; search, status / model / date filters, sort, group-by; a row opens to the description, his own words, sources, branch and PR, and its feature matrix. Adds a permanent Build item to every context menu listing every build page. Data: data/asks.jsonl (seed) mirrored to the data folder; asks.mjs add | set-status | list keeps it current.

entries.label: Build orchestrator
entries.description: Breaks every build into small steps (30 min or less), each pinned to Fable or Opus, and runs the build pipeline (Brett, Nov 8 2026): every build gets an id and a Claude split (Fable only where needed) and sits in Pending; Brett moves it to the Queue; the dispatcher (pipeline.mjs on the VPS, every minute) watches the Claude accounts (which have Fable, parallel per account) and the agent slots and, when a slot is free, starts a headless session for the next Queue build on an account that runs its next phase's model. The only place that browses and manages builds (Brett, Nov 10 2026; the Build manager is retired): tabs Pending, Queue (each build's steps, planned model and account), Active, Incomplete, Complete, Errors, then Accounts (health every 5 minutes: sign-in, credits, Fable), All builds, Approvals and Rules. When a build's turn comes the dispatcher makes the final account pick, subscriptions first (in Brett's order), then any API account, moving on until one accepts, and records which account took it. Tracker is the one builds store, _claude/builds/store.json, so any session or account continues the build (orchestrator.mjs next | brief | act; pipeline.mjs status | queue | unqueue | split | tick).

entries.label: Builds
entries.description: One Builds page over the one builds store (builds@1, owned by the Build orchestrator): every build of the active build profile, with switchable views. Builds = one row per build with a live progress bar, status, steps, time left; double-tap or right-click a name to rename it (the id never changes). Steps = every atomic step as its own stored record, for one build or the whole profile: expandable rows, multi-select (Ctrl+click, long-press, optional checkboxes), drag to reorder steps and builds, divide a step, harvest selected steps into one new build or split them into N, Restore default. Everything in the Steps view is a draft (saved, survives a restart) until Apply; Discard drops it. Live progress bars per build, per step and per profile; the banner shows the profile's percentage, animated while a build runs. Runs in AmberX too (its server forwards the routes).

entries.label: Changes & features grid
entries.description: One grid of every change (the Codebase changes log, read through axf.changes@1) and every feature (the plan). Each row is titled with its thread / request name and its date and time, and expands to show the details: what was asked, steps, result, branch, commits and links for a change; status, summary, ports, files, acceptance and history for a feature. Filter changes / features / both, search, sort.

entries.label: Chat viewer
entries.description: Every session we have, stored as transcripts (session@1) in one searchable store: claude.ai text and voice chats (from the data export Brett uploads, or the hub drop folder claude.ai sessions write to when he says "sync my chats"), Claude Code sessions (~/.claude/projects, synced incrementally on a timer and on load) and headless build sessions (build logs). Checks for updates on load (new, continued, changed, unchanged), keeps every version, redacts secrets on ingest, full-text search that jumps to the hit, chat bubbles (Brett vs Amber) with collapsible tool calls, copy / share / export as text or Markdown, and audio export with two voices (free Piper voices on the VPS by default, OpenAI or ElevenLabs when a key is saved), rendered in the background with chapters per hour and stored on the hub. Also in AmberX as Chats.

entries.label: Claude accounts
entries.description: Claude accounts on the VPS: lists the saved logins and API keys, switches the console's account, and routes headless jobs: every subscription login is a worker (the console's account takes jobs after them), 3 build and 5 wait per account, and API-key accounts take only the jobs a routing rule sends them, under daily and weekly spend caps with alerts. Job routing settings: rules on job type, model, size, priority, profile and a subscriptions-busy fallback, in order, each on or off, with a test-a-job preview. Never shows a credential. Every switch, save, sign-in or removal is one held axHub call.

entries.label: Claude
entries.description: Claude settings (claude-settings@1): settings for Claude itself, kept on axHub (/projects/_shared/_data/claude/settings.json) so every Claude session (voice, chat, Claude Code, headless agents) reads the same values at its start and before acting (MCP claude_settings_get, CLI claude-settings.mjs). Groups: No wait (owner-only: Brett's own click turns on a standing all-scope veto pass so held calls run at once; Include irreversible, duration 1 h / 4 h / until off, auto-off at night; banner chip while on; off revokes the pass at once), Follow Amber (the same switch the follow-amber build reads), Builds (default model, launch without asking, max parallel, per-build and daily budget caps, named agent locked on, UI Review gate), Verification, Talking, Notifications, Memory and notes. Open registry: a new setting is data (registry.json, registry.d/, or the hub's claude/registry.json). Owner-only settings change only from Brett's signed-in console session; sessions and agents can change the rest. Page + Settings → Plugins → Claude; 'Claude settings' in every context menu.

entries.label: Codebase changes banner
entries.description: Every time Claude is asked to build, edit, remove or fix something, an entry is opened (by a Claude Code hook) with what was asked, broken into steps that Claude fills in as it works, and the result when it's done (branch, commits, files, tests, links). A Codebase changes banner on every console load lists the entries you haven't closed; closing one clears it on every device. The permanent log lives on axHub (/projects/amberx-axf/_data/changes) and is browsable under Builds → Codebase changes.

entries.label: Context menu designer
entries.description: Design context menus: create, edit, name, rename and save them, and make 'chunks' (reusable pieces of a menu, saved from any menu with Save as chunk) that you insert into menus by name; chunks can hold items, separators and other chunks. Every menu and chunk carries its own style (font, size, weight, style, text / background colour, hover text / background colour); a chunk inherits the menu's style or uses its own. A floating live preview re-renders on every change. A saved menu becomes a standard context-menu asset (ctxd-<id>) you pick in Appearance or with Use as the context menu. Designs are kept on the console server (0600).

entries.label: Crew
entries.description: Every agent working right now, live: avatar, status (working / waiting on approval / stuck / idle), build and step in plain English, model, a timer since the job and the step started, live cost and tokens, files touched and the PR. A row opens to what the agent is doing this second (from its tool calls), the step list, every file it created, changed or deleted with the live diff against the build's base, its recent tool calls with their cost, links to its Terminal tab and session, and Stop. Idle crew sit in Off the clock; a totals bar shows who is working and what it costs. Zero tokens: plain code reading the headless logs, the builds store and git.

entries.label: Fable rebuilds

entries.label: Feature matrix
entries.description: Every build gets a feature matrix (feature-matrix@1): grouped items, each with its minutes, model (Fable / Opus) and why; tick = keep, untick = skip; items can be added any time and are never deleted. All matrices are one dataset, shown as a grid of expandable rows (row = build: profile, date added, time cost of the kept items, kept / skipped, needs apply, last applied). Editing lights Apply, which pushes the totals, skips and estimates to every table the build lives in (orchestrator, pending list, build queue, build manager / change log, plan) through the framework's Apply engine. Every builds grid gets a row button and a right-click 'Feature matrix' (lib-datagrid row hooks). Files: _claude/builds/[profiles/<id>/]matrices.json, mirrored to the plugin data folder.

entries.label: Maintenance
entries.description: Server health and safe clean-up for the VPS (maintenance@1). A dashboard of disk, memory, swap, load, Docker images, volumes and build cache, build worktrees, logs and /tmp, with the biggest space users. Clean-up jobs (finished build worktrees, dangling Docker images and build cache, old logs, /tmp leftovers, containers stuck in Created) always preview first, then go to axHub as one held call: nothing is removed until Brett approves it, and the VPS re-checks every item before removing it. Never running containers, volumes in use or app data. Nightly auto-clean of the safe jobs (off by default), alerts at 80/85/90% disk and when swap stays nearly full (console and phone), the systems check row Server health with Auto fix, and a Server disk card for Home (server health is plain code, no AI). Clean up build profiles: audits every build profile (open builds, steps, copied tracker checklists and plans) against merged PRs, git history, reports, the catalog and the other profiles; each item gets keep / done already / not needed / duplicate / merge with a reason and proof. Preview first, untick anything, then apply: done → complete, the rest archived (never deleted), one undo per run, running builds never touched. Deep (AI) mode when a model is set up, Basic (exact matches) otherwise.

entries.label: MD Studio
entries.description: A Markdown browser and editor for every .md file Brett works with, on the dock engine. A column lists the files in collapsible categories by scope (Project, Claude, Repo, Notes Vault) with an edit switch per file and its reference chain as branches; files open as dock tabs that float, split, resize and drop on any tab header or into a split. Preview, edit or split with live preview, a Markdown toolbar, find and replace, autosave, conflict-safe saves and version history with restore. Four views (Browse, Read, Write, IDE), snippets to drag in, wizards for Claude md files, and a context view with token counts per referenced part.

entries.label: Notes

Folders and notes on the left, the rendered note on the right; search, sort by date or name, new note, rename, move between folders, delete (confirmed, history kept on the hub) and an edit switch that saves only when nobody else changed the note. entries.label: Plugin commands

Merge queue view, banner chip, REST + MCP + CLI. 0.7.1 (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "Stop merging these things one at a time"): auto-land is off by default and only the merge queue merges AmberX-AXF; GitHub reads are cached with ETags (a 304 costs no API call) and held back when the shared limit runs low; the console redeploys once per stack.

entries.description: Every UI a build makes comes here for Brett's approval, one section per kind (open registry: Design packs, Whole apps / programs, Screens & pages, Settings interfaces, Dialogs & popups, Menus & toolbars, Banners & cards, Other). Each item carries its app, build, branch and PR, desktop + phone screenshots, notes, a status (waiting, approved, changes asked, rejected), his comment and its history. entries.label: VPS
entries.description: The one server everything runs on (Hostinger VPS, Coolify, Traefik, the console), through axHub's VPS connector. Every action here is an allow-listed command (the entries are the allow-list): the registry validates each value and shell-quotes it into a fixed template, and axHub's vps.run asks Brett before anything runs. Destructive ones (stop, restart, kill, reboot, prune) also need the registry's confirm token. Power and backups at Hostinger level: hostinger/tool/vps.
